html:
The partitions of Poland were the three steps, in 1772, 1793 and 1795, by which Russia, Prussia and Austria divided the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth between them until it ceased to exist.

The Commonwealth was weak, its parliament often blocked by a single veto, and Russia already controlled its kings. The first partition followed a noble revolt. Reformers answered with the Constitution of 3 May 1791, but Russia invaded and took more land in the second partition. The rising of Tadeusz Kościuszko in 1794 was crushed, and the third partition ended the state. Poles kept their nation alive in exile, in culture and in risings such as the November Uprising, until Poland was reborn in 1918. See also Partitions of Poland.
sum: The partitions of Poland were the three steps, in 1772, 1793 and 1795, by which Russia, Prussia and Austria divided the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth between them until it ceased to exist.
